newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian Rietumu optimistic on Unibanka shares.
newsitem.headline: Latvian Rietumu optimistic on Unibanka shares.

text.p: Latvian bank Rietumu Bank said on Friday it was optimistic for more gains in the shares of stock market blue chip Unibanka and that bourse newcomer Valmiera Glassfibre would also gain.
The bank said in a research note that during the last five days Unibanka has risen to 3.91 lats from 3.28 lats, which it said was reasonable as Unibanka was the cheapest of the Baltic banking stocks.
"There is at the moment a big potential for a rise (in Unibanka)," Rietumu said. It also noted that the forthcoming Unibanka shareholders on March 25 was also having an influence.
Unibanka shareholders are expected at the meeting to back a merger with Zemes Bank and to approve plans for 1997 and review the profits for 1996.
Rietumu also said that bourse newcomer, Valmiera Glassfibre, should rise from its planned nominal listing price of one lat to between 1.60 lats to 1.70 lats.
Germany's Glasseiden Oschatz has a 49 percent stake in Valmiera Glassfibre, which made a 235,736 lat 1996 profit and had assets of 14.08 million lats.
It said the company was interesting as a medium and long-term investment as it had a high technological production base, sold most of its product in the West and had a Western investor.
